angles.drive: Giving is your first language. You would rather hand over your help than wait to see whether it was wanted, since being needed is how you feel sure of your place. Keep some of it back for the people who ask.

You make things slowly by choice, and the slow ones last. You enjoy the making more than the finishing, and your best things take years and hold for a long time. Let one out before it feels complete, since lasting work also needs its day.

You are happy with enough and mean it. Since more never felt like the point, you would rather enjoy a good day than work toward a better one. Keep one wish that enough does not cover, because contentment also needs somewhere to go.

You give the way you breathe, without checking the supply. You feel safe only while you are needed, and you keep giving rather than stop long enough to notice you are tired. You know the tiredness is a message, and it is addressed to you.

You drift along because drifting is pleasant. You are never in a hurry, so you would rather let the day carry you than steer it. You know drifting is not the same as resting, and only one of them puts anything back.

You are too soft on everyone in reach, and you enjoy it. Because comfort feels like proof you are needed, you soften everything rather than hand over the version worth growing into. Bear in mind that ease is only half of what you give.

Your warmth arrives in generous portions, seconds included. The laugh is real and audible from the driveway, the welcome fills doorways, the food comes in servings that assume everyone is recovering from something. People leave your presence heavier and lighter at the same time.

Contentment came to you early and never left. The house is enough, the work is enough, tonight’s dinner is a small event worth savoring out loud. Peace like yours reads as quietly radical among people who are permanently mid-upgrade.

Feeding people, literally and otherwise, is your default expression of everything. Congratulations come as dinner, condolences as casserole, apology as pie. Words were never quite your instrument. The stocked plate says what you mean with better grammar than you ever found.

Good enough arrived years ago and you parked there. The skills plateaued where the applause got comfortable, the menu settled into rotation, the questions you ask the world got smaller. Nothing is wrong. That is the anesthetic, and it is working.

Your engine idles low, and everything discretionary waits behind it. The reply sits, the errand rolls to next week, the project gathers a soft dust. It is never refusal, just a body that treats urgency as a rumor and momentum as an occasional guest.

Comfort is your climate, and discomfort gets treated as a system error. The thermostat, the cushions, the snacks within reach of the good chair: your setup absorbs effort before effort forms. Convenience was the reward once. Somewhere along the way it became the requirement.
